# Mii-Style Rendering & Content-Pack Conventions

Read this before implementing any mii-style-visual-overhaul issue so every
step makes the same choices. Plan: `.claude/plans/mii-style-visual-overhaul.md`.

## The three invariants

1. **One shared pool.** NPCs, the creator, and the player avatar all draw
   from `partCatalog()`/`paletteCatalog()` via `drawCompositeCharacter`.
   Never add a parts source or a renderer variant for one consumer — that
   reintroduces the pool-separation bug PR #99 removed.
2. **Style is data.** Proportions = `localSize`/sockets on catalog rows.
   Colors = palette rows. Pack membership = the `pack` tag. If a change
   requires editing assembly code (`assembleLook`) or picker logic to look
   different, the design is wrong — stop and re-read the plan.
3. **Contracts hold.** Sockets resolve unscaled, ONE uniform scale to the
   1.8u height contract afterward; style tags (round/blocky/any) gate every
   combination; `hair_none`-style explicit zero-size parts instead of
   missing slots.

## Graphics-pack seam (step 1)

A pack is: catalog rows (`pack: "tag"`) + palettes (`pack: "tag"`) +
renderer recipes for its part ids. Nothing else. The recipe dispatch in
`RaylibRenderer.cpp` must be a single function with signature roughly
`drawPartRecipe(const PartDef&, Vec3 at, Vec3 dim, const Colors&)` so a
future pack extends one dispatch site. The generic declared-box fallback
stays the safety net for any part without a bespoke recipe.

## Inverted-hull outlines (step 3)

- Re-issue the same part draws FIRST, scaled ~1.05 about each part's
  center, in near-black (`{30, 30, 36}` family), with
  `rlSetCullFace(RL_CULL_FACE_FRONT)`; restore `RL_CULL_FACE_BACK` after.
- `rlgl` state calls flush the batch — group the outline pass, then the
  color pass, not interleaved per part.
- Boxes are the known risk (corner gaps). Escalation order: bump hull
  scale → per-recipe outline opt-out flag → (logged, last resort) skip
  outlines on box parts only. Never abandon outlines globally without a
  screenshot comparison in OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md.
- Screenshot-verify on BOTH a sphere-family and box-family character.

## Mii proportion targets (step 2)

Head ≈ 40–45% of standing height (Tomodachi reference). Bodies shorten to
~0.75–0.85u, heads grow to ~0.95–1.05u, sockets re-authored per part.
Yardstick: the cop close-up shot from PR #99
(`docs/qa/screenshots/shared-character-library/qa_shot_cop.png`) is the
"before"; the "after" head should read roughly twice as dominant.

## Mouth category + look format (step 4)

Land as ONE commit: enum + count bump, CategorySpec row (`Mouth`→`Head`
via `"mouth"`), `mouth` sockets on all heads, ≥4 mouth parts + recipes,
Menu `categoryLabel` case. Look format: `look = body, head, eyes, hair,
mouth, palette` (six items); the five-item form MUST keep parsing (mouth
via the deterministic fallback) so shipped persona files and stored looks
never break. `renderPersonaText` always emits six.

## Player avatar (step 6)

Reserved id `player_avatar` in the existing CharacterStore look table — no
new storage. The creator page runs in "avatar mode" (same picker/Randomize/
preview; Save writes the avatar row instead of spawning). First-person
visibility: tint the punch sleeve/fist and pistol hand from the avatar's
palette in `drawViewmodel`. Remote-player replication is OUT of scope
(logged seam; guests still see rigged meshes).

## Verification recipe

`caffeinate -u -t 3` then
`./build/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs --frames 90 shot.png --camera <x> <z> <yaw> --hour 12`
— the PNG lands in CWD regardless of path given. Read the PNG. Suite:
`make -C tests test` (un-skip the matching stub in `tests/test_style_pack.cpp`
in the same commit as each step).
---

=== personas/cop.persona ===
name = Officer Dana Brooks
role = beat cop posted outside the City Police Station
traits = dry-humored, observant, by-the-book but fair, secretly soft-hearted
style = clipped, 1-2 sentences, police shorthand, deadpan jokes
knowledge = Knows every corner of downtown, the shop owners by name, and the usual petty complaints: pigeons at the fountain, Ray's cab parked too long, skateboarders by the library. Nothing about other cities or world events.
spot = police
position = 0, -36
facing = 0
look = body_block, head_block, eyes_visor, hair_cap, mouth_neutral, slate
armed = true
---
You stand watch in front of the station on the south side of downtown,
across from Marge's Bakery, where you buy rye bread every Friday.
Answer questions like an incident report: short, factual, slightly amused.
If someone seems lost, point them toward the plaza fountain in the middle of
town. Never discuss open cases; there aren't any anyway, and that bores you.

=== personas/baker.persona ===
name = Marge Holloway
role = bakery owner at Marge's Bakery
traits = warm, gossipy, fiercely proud of her sourdough, motherly
style = 1-3 short sentences, motherly, drops baking metaphors
knowledge = Knows the downtown blocks, her regulars, and everything about bread. Knows Officer Brooks buys rye every Friday and that Theo at Bean There Coffee burns his espresso. Nothing about world news or technology.
spot = bakery
position = -70, -36
facing = 0
look = body_pear, head_round, eyes_happy, hair_bun, mouth_smile, warm
schedule = 5-12, -70, -36, baking bread
schedule = 12-14, -8, -6, lunch at the plaza
schedule = 14-20, -70, -36, selling loaves
schedule = 20-5, -70, -36, closing up
---
You run the bakery on the southwest corner of downtown. The police station is
just across the street to the east, and you can smell Bean There Coffee two
blocks over when the wind is right.
Greet strangers like future regulars and try to guess what they'd order.
If asked for directions, give them in terms of shops and smells, not street
names. Complain gently about the 5 a.m. starts.

=== personas/librarian.persona ===
name = Ms. Adaeze Obi
role = head librarian at the City Library
traits = precise, well-read, quietly witty, protective of quiet
style = measured full sentences, 1-3 per reply, occasional literary references
knowledge = Knows the library's collection, local history of the downtown blocks, and which regulars never return books (Mr. Whitfield, lovingly). Knows the layout of every street downtown. Nothing about the internet; the card catalogue is authority enough.
spot = library
position = -36, 0
facing = 90
look = body_slim, head_oval, eyes_glasses, hair_bob, mouth_neutral, mono
---
You take your breaks on the library steps on the west side of downtown,
facing the plaza. The fountain noise carries; you don't mind it.
Recommend a (fictional, plausible) book for whatever topic comes up.
If asked for directions, give them precisely, in cardinal directions and
paces. Gently shush anyone who uses too many exclamation points.

=== personas/musician.persona ===
name = Benny "Strings" Malone
role = street musician busking at the edge of the park
traits = laid-back, poetic, broke but unbothered, hears music in everything
style = mellow 1-3 sentences, musical metaphors, occasionally rhymes without meaning to
knowledge = Knows every song anyone has ever requested, the acoustics of every downtown corner, and that the fountain in the plaza hums in B-flat. Theo from the coffee shop sneaks him free espresso. Doesn't know or care what day of the week it is.
spot = park
position = 52, 52
facing = 225
look = body_block, head_tall, eyes_wink, hair_mohawk, mouth_smile, cool
schedule = 10-16, 10, -10, busking at the plaza
schedule = 16-23, 52, 52, playing for the park

All screenshots are saved. Here is my full QA report.

## JOB 1 — Consistency Gate

**Verdict: PASS WITH CAVEATS**

- **Mii proportions everywhere** — PASS. Verified via both code (`CategorySpec`/socket math in `src/core/CharacterParts.cpp`: head fraction of total assembled height computes to ~49% for `body_block`+`head_block`, similarly generous for round bodies) and direct pixel measurement on `baker_closeup.png` (head ~60% of figure), `player_char_closeup.png` (head ~65%), and `musician_closeup4.png` (head ~60%, box family). No old-proportioned figure found anywhere.
- **Dark outline rims on every character, spheres and boxes, no glaring hull artifacts** — PASS for the actual composite geometry. Zoomed crops of round heads (baker, player character) and box heads/bodies (musician, cop's real head+torso once separated from the emote overlay — see caveat) all show a single, crisp, unbroken black rim with clean corners; no double edges, no gaps, no flicker bands. **CAVEAT:** a pre-existing, non-Mii legacy system — the per-mood "emote billboard" (`RaylibRenderer.cpp` ~line 582, `DrawBillboard(... faceTexture(face) ...)` at fixed height 2.45) — draws a flat, un-outlined circular face floating above the composite head whenever `mood != Neutral`. It visually reads as a second, disconnected head with none of the new outline/style treatment. Because the documented capture recipe requires `--frames N`, which sets `smokeRun = true` and forces `face = i % 6` (main.cpp line 1064), **5 of every 6 NPCs will show this artifact in any screenshot taken the documented way** — confirmed on `cop_closeup2.png`/`cop_fullbody.png` (Angry emote) vs. `musician_closeup4.png` (index lands on Neutral, no emote, clean head visible). This also fires in normal gameplay whenever an NPC's mood shifts, not just in scripted runs.
- **Mouths visible on faces at close range** — PASS. Confirmed on baker (flat neutral-ish bar), player character (smile bar+dots), musician (bar+dots), all legible at close range.
- **Pastel palette cohesion** — PASS. Every screenshot (plaza, street, park, night, morning) shows the same warm-peach-skin / muted-hair / saturated-pastel-outfit family; nothing reads as an asset from another game.
- **Player-created character indistinguishable from townsfolk** — PASS. `custom_1783494792_10` (position 0, 8) uses `body_round/head_oval/eyes_happy/hair_none/mint`, same catalog, sockets, scale contract, and outline pass as authored NPCs (side-by-side with a bystander NPC in `player_char_closeup.png`). Its stored `look_json` predates the Mouth category and has no `"mouth"` key; the documented fallback (`mouth_smile` default in `CharacterLook::fromJson`) resolves this correctly and it visually reads as an intentional smile.

## JOB 2 — Free Playtest Sweep

1. The legacy mood-emote billboard (see above) is the single biggest thing undercutting "one cohesive art source" in practice — it has no outline, a different flat-shaded style, and floats disconnected above the actual Mii head. Worth reconciling now that composite heads have real mouths (e.g., retire it for composite characters, or restyle/outline it to match).
2. Night (hour 23, `late_night.png`) darkens the sky and buildings uniformly but has zero lit windows or streetlamp glow — it reads as "daytime scene with a dark filter" rather than a lived-in night city.
3. Dusk (hour 20, `night_scene.png`) washes the *entire* frame — sky, buildings, ground — in one flat rust-orange tint, which looks more like a dust storm/fog event than a sunset; worth checking the color-grading curve at that hour.
4. The plaza (`plaza_wide.png`) is a huge flat beige plane with only 2-3 NPCs and almost no props; the park (`park_scene.png`) is just a fountain + bench + two potted plants on empty grass, reusing what looks like the same fountain asset as the plaza — neither space reads as distinct or lived-in.
5. Street clutter placement looks arbitrary: a cardboard box and a lone shrub sit in open tan ground between sidewalk and buildings with no clear relationship to any storefront/dumpster (`street_scene.png`).
6. Building facades are visually repetitive — nearly every building reuses the identical window-grid module, just palette-swapped; downtown reads as one building repeated rather than several designs.
7. Roads are very wide (6+ lanes plus crosswalks) relative to the tightly-clustered, pedestrian-scaled storefronts and sparse traffic (0-2 cars per shot), making streets feel oversized and empty.
8. NPCs mostly stand in small idle clusters on open pavement rather than interacting with the environment (no one at a bench, shop entrance, or in a conversational pose), so the town feels more like "figures parked in a lot" than street life.
9. `mouth_smile`'s raised end-dots read as "flat bar with two dots" rather than a clear upturned smile at typical screenshot distance — it satisfies "mouth visible" but the *smile* read specifically is weak; a slight upward curve might sell it better.
10. Street furniture variety is thin — potted plants and traffic signals are the only repeated prop types across plaza/street/park; 1-2 more prop types would help ped-level variety.

## Best 3 Screenshots

- `docs/qa/screenshots/mii-style/musician_closeup4.png` — clean box-family head+body, full outline with no artifacts, no emote contamination (best single proof of Mii proportions/outline quality for the blocky family).
- `docs/qa/screenshots/mii-style/baker_closeup.png` — clean sphere/round-family head+body, full outline, mouth clearly visible.
- `docs/qa/screenshots/mii-style/player_char_closeup.png` — the player-created character in the foreground next to a bystander NPC, demonstrating construction parity (and incidentally showing two instances of the emote-billboard caveat in the background).
